# Best luxury buyers’ advocates in Adelaide

For prestige homes in Adelaide, I’d shortlist firms that can do more than find properties: they should provide discreet acquisition advice, access to suitable off-market opportunities, rigorous property valuation, skilled negotiation and end-to-end due diligence.

My research suggests a useful distinction between **specialist luxury-property advisers** and **independent buyers’ agents**\. The former may offer a stronger prestige-market network and a tailored service; the latter can be particularly valuable for independent price assessment and representing your interests exclusively as the buyer.

Adelaide’s prestige market has a relatively limited supply of exceptional properties, and recent industry commentary points to increasing activity in sales above \$5 million, including off-market transactions. That makes local relationships and the ability to assess a property's true value especially important. ## What to check before engaging anyone

For a high-value purchase, I would ask each shortlisted firm the same questions\:

- **Comparable acquisitions\:** How many homes have you acquired in my target price bracket over the past two years? Can you provide references from recent clients?
- **Off-market access\:** What recent prestige properties have you sourced before public listing, and how do you establish that the price is fair?
- **Valuation\:** Will I receive a written assessment using comparable sales, land value, building condition and any relevant heritage or planning constraints?
- **Conflicts\:** Do you exclusively represent the buyer on this transaction? Disclose any relationships with selling agents, developers or other parties.
- **Fees\:** Is the fee fixed, percentage-based or success-based? What is included, and are there additional charges?
- **Due diligence\:** Who coordinates building and pest inspections, title and easement checks, planning reviews and independent conveyancing advice?

The REBAA directory is a useful additional check for membership, relevant experience, licensing and recent client references. [rebaa.com.au](https://rebaa.com.au/location/sa/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

search_results.title: Offers flood in for Mount Schank ex-post office near volcano
search_results.description: A historic 7.98-hectare property located at 137 Post Office Rd, Mount Schank, South Australia, has garnered significant interest shortly after being listed for sale. Selling agent Jason Malseed of Malseeds Real Estate reports that the former Mount Schank post office, situated atop a 100m-high dormant volcano about 12km south of Mount Gambier, has attracted some of the highest inquiry levels in his 40-plus-year career. The property, priced between $499,000 and $539,000, has already received several strong offers, including one for $540,000. Built in 1890, the three-bedroom home served as a post office and telephone exchange intermittently until 1984 and was home to notable local families, including the Ashbys. The property, which is not heritage-listed but within a 150-hectare state heritage area, draws interest largely due to the volcano's fertile soils and the home’s renovation potential. Most of the over 50 inquiries have come from local buyers interested in restoring the historic building, despite a few suggesting demolition. The property was last occupied by a 90-year-old woman who passed away the previous year and is now being sold by her son.

search_results.title: SA's Louth Island attracts buyers keen on private getaway
search_results.description: Louth Island, a rare privately-owned freehold island near Port Lincoln, South Australia, has garnered significant interest since hitting the market, with over 100 inquiries, including at least 15 potential buyers looking to transform it into a private holiday retreat. Formerly a sheep station, the island was acquired for $2.5 million in 2021 by Uniti Wireless co-founder Che Metcalfe and his wife Natasha. They invested $30 million to develop a luxury eco-resort, Rumi on Louth, featuring upscale accommodations for 20 guests and the acclaimed Samphire Restaurant. However, business operations paused in May 2026 as the couple reconsidered future plans, despite approvals for a $20 million second-stage expansion including 43 new villas, a second restaurant, a day spa, and recreational facilities. Some international interests have expressed intent to simply hold the asset, while others are keen on completing the development. No specific price guide has been set, but comparisons draw to Hamilton Island's $1.2 billion sale, underscoring Louth Island’s premium value. As one of Australia's few privately-held islands without leasehold risks, the property offers multiple beaches and exclusive ownership appeal. Expressions of interest close Wednesday.

search_results.title: Construction starts on Adelaide apartments One Four Four Hutt
search_results.description: Construction has officially commenced on the One Four Four Hutt apartment development in Adelaide, a joint venture between Fortis and Otello. The 10-storey building, designed by DKO and located on a 1241sqm corner site, will include a mix of one, two, and three-bedroom residences, including a penthouse collection, plus 400sqm of ground-floor retail space. All one-bedroom units have already been sold, with two- and three-bedroom apartments still available starting at $1.125 million and $2.099 million respectively. To date, 19 unconditional sales have been secured, totaling approximately $25.9 million, with an additional four units reserved. Fortis head of development Arthur Dendrinos emphasized the strong demand for premium living in Adelaide, noting this milestone underscores Fortis' long-term commitment to the region. Otello director Daniel Harris highlighted the project's positive impact on the Hutt Street precinct and expressed confidence in the appointed builder, BLAG Commercial, citing a successful previous partnership.

search_results.title: Construction starts on Onkaparinga Heights' Edenridge estate
search_results.description: Construction has commenced on the Edenridge estate in Onkaparinga Heights, marking the first stage of a masterplanned community projected to eventually accommodate up to 900 families. The initial phase will deliver 45 homes, targeting first-time buyers and young families, with completion expected by April 2027. The development, led by YAS Property & Development, is situated on a 100-hectare site elevated 150 meters above sea level, adjacent to Onkaparinga River National Park. The suburb, formerly part of Hackham, was rezoned and renamed in 2023. Alongside Edenridge, a separate 1000-home development by Lanser, selected by Renewal SA, will begin civil works in late 2027 on a nearby 67.6-hectare parcel. At least 20% of these homes will be designated as affordable housing under the HomeSeekerSA initiative. Combined, the two projects will bring nearly 2000 new homes to the Onkaparinga City Council area. Designed with a focus on lifestyle and environmental integration, Edenridge promises enhanced green spaces and increased tree canopy, offering residents direct access to the national park and promoting a nature-connected living environment.

search_results.title: Prestige property SA: Top agents reveal luxury home buying secrets
search_results.description:
This article compiles insights from South Australia's top real estate agents on effectively buying and selling prestige properties. Luxury real estate demands a tailored approach, emphasizing high-end marketing strategies, professional presentation, and agent alignment with the property's prestige. Experts stress that luxury buyers seek finished homes with standout features like pools, wine rooms, large master suites, and space for multi-generational living. Five-bedroom homes with studies are in high demand.

Prestige buyers value large landholdings in premium areas, character homes with modern renovations, or architecturally designed new builds. Professionally styled, furnished homes boost emotional appeal and sale price. Agents recommend open inspections for accessibility and caution against off-market sales, which might miss broader demand and stronger offers. 

School zones significantly affect property value, and while auctions can drive competition, the method should depend on expected buyer interest. Pools may be attractive to family buyers but are not universally beneficial. Pricing transparency and realistic renovation plans are advised. The current market favors sellers due to limited stock. Ultimately, timing, staging, and employing an experienced agent are key to success in the luxury property market.
